name: career-compass-mcp
description: Your AI-native career co-pilot — Career KB, tailored resumes, job pipeline, interview prep, and offer evaluation. Local-first: your data never leaves your machine.
long_description:
Career Compass turns Claude into a full job-search partner. It keeps your entire career history as plain YAML on your own disk, then uses it to tailor a resume to any posting, score your fit, draft cover letters, track every application from discovery through offer, prep you for each interview with STAR stories drawn from your real work, and evaluate offers against your targets.

It is local-first by design. There is no account, no cloud sync, and no telemetry. The whole package makes exactly one outbound network request: check_setup asks the public npm registry whether a newer version has been released, which sends nothing about you or your data and is skipped entirely when you call it with checkForUpdates: false. Your career data lives in a folder you choose and is passed only to the Claude client you connect, only for the requests you make.

Includes a dependency-free local dashboard (kanban pipeline, per-application detail, stage-distribution chart) that re-reads your YAML on every request.

tools.name: explore_opportunity
tools.description: Analyze a job posting against your Career KB and your stated preferences — salary band, remote/relocation, notice period. Returns an honest fit verdict (checked against the job board's own label, if you supply it), matched strengths, gaps, talking points, and a 'day in the life' brief.

tools.name: research_company
tools.description: Build an intelligence brief on a company: product, funding, culture, tech stack, interview process, and strategic fit with your goals.

tools.name: tailor_resume
tools.description: Generate a tailored, ATS-optimized resume matched to a specific job posting using your Career KB.

tools.name: generate_cover_letter
tools.description: Write a compelling, personalized cover letter for a specific job posting using your Career KB.

tools.name: format_for_ats
tools.description: Format resume and application content for specific ATS systems: Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, LinkedIn, and others.

tools.name: pipeline_view
tools.description: Read the job application pipeline: list applications, summarize stats, surface what needs attention, or fetch one application by id. Read-only — never modifies anything.

tools.name: pipeline_add
tools.description: Add one job application to the pipeline. Creates a new record; never modifies an existing one. Use pipeline_update to change an application already being tracked.

tools.name: pipeline_update
tools.description: Update one application already in the pipeline: change its status, add a note, set a follow-up date, record a contact, or log an interview round. Overwrites the fields you supply and leaves the rest untouched.

tools.name: classify_email
tools.description: Classify a job-search-related email and extract structured data: type, company, role, contact, next action, and urgency.

tools.name: prepare_interview
tools.description: Generate comprehensive interview prep: STAR stories, likely questions, company alignment, and bridge topics — tailored to interview type.

tools.name: interview_arc
tools.description: Mid-process projection: reconstructs the interview arc so far — rounds completed, what each surfaced, threads left open — then projects what the NEXT round will probe, without repeating ground already covered.

tools.name: evaluate_offer
tools.description: Analyze a job offer: break down total compensation, compare to market, build negotiation strategy, and draft counter scripts.

tools.name: ingest_document
tools.description: Paste any career document — performance review, award email, project summary, LinkedIn recommendation — and extract structured achievements for your Career KB. Extraction only: it reads what you paste and returns YAML for review. Writing that YAML to disk is a separate, explicit step with save_career_section.

tools.name: generate_rejection_response
tools.description: Craft a graceful rejection response that keeps the door open, maintains relationships, and positions you for future opportunities. If you pass applicationId, this also sets that application's status to `rejected` in your pipeline — it does not only write a draft.

tools.name: capture_insight
tools.description: Record a durable career signal to your journal — what an interview surfaced, why an offer felt right or wrong, the pattern behind a rejection, fresh proof of a skill. Append-only; over time these compound into the real shape of your career and enrich future resume, interview, and fit work.

tools.name: save_career_section
tools.description: Write one section of the Career KB to disk. This is how the Career KB gets populated — ingest_document and the resume tools only read and extract. Replaces the whole section, so send the complete list you want stored, not just new entries. The previous version is kept as a timestamped .bak next to it.

tools.name: harvest_evidence
tools.description: Read a local project's git history and report what you measurably did there — months active, files and file types touched, your share of commits, test ratio — each with the command that produced it. Use it when the user cannot remember what they shipped, is writing a résumé bullet for a project, or needs proof of a skill. It reports counts and asks the questions a commit log cannot answer; it never invents achievements and never writes to the Career KB.

tools.name: check_setup
tools.description: Health-check this Career Compass install and report everything at once: whether a newer version has shipped, whether your data directory exists and is writable, which Career KB sections are filled in, whether the pipeline file parses, leftover temp files, and whether the dashboard is running. Every finding comes with the one command that fixes it. Run this first whenever something seems wrong, or right after an install or upgrade.

career_data_path.title: Career data folder
career_data_path.description: Where your career history and job pipeline are stored, as plain YAML. Nothing is uploaded — this folder never leaves your machine. Leave the default unless you want it somewhere specific, such as inside a folder you already back up.
